text: Hue attracts over $1 billion in new registered capital in 11 months
According to a report presented at the November regular meeting of the Hue City People ' s Committee, the central city ' s socio-economic performance continued to show broad-based gains.

In the first 11 months of 2026, tourist arrivals were estimated at 7.28 million, up 24.6 percent year on year, while tourism revenue surged 57.3 percent to VND18.47 trillion ($727 million), remaining a key growth driver for the local service sector.
Industrial production rose 14 percent over the same period, led by an 18.6 percent increase in manufacturing and processing.
Export turnover was estimated at $1.63 billion, up 22.4 percent, while total retail sales of goods and consumer service revenue reached VND71.56 trillion ($2.82 billion), up 19.3 percent.

During the 11-month period, Hue licensed 48 new projects with total registered capital of VND25.43 trillion ($1 billion) and approved capital increases for 16 existing projects adding VND2.8 trillion ($110 million).

State budget revenue reached an estimated VND15.25 trillion ($600 million), fulfilling 95.3 percent of the city's annual target and rising 18.2 percent year on year, positioning the city close to its full-year target of VND16 trillion ($630 million).
Alongside economic indicators, labor and social welfare remained priorities.
The city created jobs for approximately 18,460 workers, while 84.1 percent of residents received at least one health check-up or screening during the year.
Administrative reform also progressed, with online public service applications reaching 93.1 percent, placing Hue among the top five localities nationwide in this metric.

Despite positive momentum, Hue faces substantial tasks in the final month of the year, particularly completing budget revenue targets, accelerating public investment disbursement, and resolving stalled projects.
Addressing the meeting, Chairman of the Hue City People's Committee Le Tri Thanh instructed departments and localities to review all assigned tasks and ensure timely, high-quality completion.

On public investment, he urged project management boards and investors to step up on-site inspections at projects at risk of delay and remove bottlenecks in site clearance, compensation, pricing, and construction, aiming to disburse 100 percent of the Prime Minister's assigned public investment plan by January 31, 2027.

On budget collection, Mr. Thanh directed tax authorities and land-use rights auction units to proactively implement approved plans to achieve the VND16 trillion ($630 million) target before December 15, 2026.
Meanwhile, the industry and trade sector and the Hue Economic and Industrial Zone s Authority were tasked with closely monitoring factory operations to support businesses ahead of 2027.

In tourism, authorities were instructed to launch immediate year-end activities to capture recovering international demand, announce the 2027 tourism event calendar early, and strengthen regional linkages with Da Nang.

To prepare for year-end and Lunar New Year demand, trade and local authorities were tasked with supporting household businesses and securing goods supply, alongside close agricultural monitoring against weather and pest risks to curb price volatility.
